title: cacheComponents
description: Learn how to enable the cacheComponents flag in Next.js.
related:

---

Cache Components enables component and function-level caching using the [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) directive. Data fetching is dynamic by default, and you choose what to cache at the page, component, or function level. Next.js prerenders a static HTML shell that is served immediately while dynamic content streams in when ready, letting you mix static and dynamic content within a single route.

## Usage

To enable the `cacheComponents` flag, set it to `true` in your `next.config.ts` file:

```ts filename="next.config.ts"
import type { NextConfig } from 'next'

const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
  cacheComponents: true,
}

export default nextConfig
```

> **Good to know**: Cache Components requires the Node.js runtime. Migrate any routes that set the deprecated `runtime = 'edge'` export, and note that other server-side JavaScript runtimes are not guaranteed to work. See [Migrating to Cache Components](/docs/app/guides/migrating-to-cache-components#runtime--edge).

When `cacheComponents` is enabled, you can use the following cache functions and configurations:

- The [`use cache` directive](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache)
- The [`cacheLife` function](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheLife) with `use cache`
- The [`cacheTag` function](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag)

> **Good to know**: If you used `experimental.useCache` or `experimental.dynamicIO`, migrate using the [Version 16 upgrade guide](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16#experimentaldynamicio-and-experimentalusecache). To migrate route segment configs and other caching patterns, see [Migrating to Cache Components](/docs/app/guides/migrating-to-cache-components).

Additionally, `cacheComponents` implements **[Partial Prerendering (PPR)](/docs/app/glossary#partial-prerendering-ppr)** as the default behavior in the App Router. This means the `experimental.ppr` configuration flag and the `experimental_ppr` route segment configuration are no longer necessary and have been removed.

Read [Prerendering](/docs/app/getting-started/caching#prerendering) for how the static shell and streaming fit together.

> **Good to know**: If you used experimental PPR in Next.js 15, refer to the [Partial Prerendering (PPR)](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16#partial-prerendering-ppr) section of the Version 16 upgrade guide when migrating.

## Navigation with Activity

When `cacheComponents` is enabled, Next.js uses React's [`<Activity>`](https://react.dev/reference/react/Activity) component to preserve component state during client-side navigation.

Rather than unmounting the previous route when you navigate away, Next.js sets the Activity mode to [`"hidden"`](https://react.dev/reference/react/Activity#activity). This means:

- Component state is preserved when navigating between routes
- When you navigate back, the previous route reappears with its state intact
- Effects are cleaned up when a route is hidden, and recreated when it becomes visible again

This behavior improves the navigation experience by maintaining UI state (form inputs, or expanded sections) when users navigate back and forth between routes.

> **Good to know**: Next.js uses heuristics to keep a few recently visited routes `"hidden"`, while older routes are removed from the DOM to prevent excessive growth.

Some UI patterns behave differently when components stay mounted instead of unmounting. See the [Preserving UI state guide](/docs/app/guides/preserving-ui-state) for handling common patterns like dropdowns, dialogs, and testing.

## Version History

| Version | Change                                                                                                                            |
| ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 16.0.0  | `cacheComponents` introduced. This flag controls the `ppr`, `useCache`, and `dynamicIO` flags as a single, unified configuration. |

With Cache Components enabled, Next.js validates in development whether navigating into each route renders instantly, and surfaces the code that would block it as an error or insight. 21 22 ## Use the adoption skill (recommended) 23 24 The [`next-cache-components-adoption`](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/tree/canary/skills/next-cache-components-adoption) skill drives this migration with a coding agent, one feature at a time, checking in at every feature boundary. It supports two modes: 25 26 - **Incremental.** Opens a single mechanical PR that opts every route out of validation, then ships each feature as a follow-up PR. This automates the [Adopting incrementally](#adopting-incrementally) flow below. 27 - **Direct.** Adopts every route in place on one branch. 28 29 Install the skill: 30 31 ```bash filename="Terminal" 32 npx skills add vercel/next.js --skill next-cache-components-adoption 33 ``` 34 35 Then give the agent this prompt: 36 37 ```prompt 38 Adopt Cache Components in this project using the next-cache-components-adoption skill. 39 ``` 40 41 ## Or migrate by hand 42 43 Migrating an existing app by hand follows a few steps, in order: 44 45 1. [Enable Cache Components](#enable-cache-components) in `next.config.ts`. 46 2. Decide your approach: convert every route now, or [adopt incrementally](#adopting-incrementally) by [opting routes out of validation](#opting-out-of-validation) first and converting one at a time. 47 3. [Follow the validation errors and insights](#following-validation) it surfaces, replacing each route segment config with its Cache Components equivalent and caching uncached data with [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) or wrapping runtime data in [``](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense). The per-key sections below cover each config and API. 48 49 Your existing `fetch` and `unstable_cache` caching keeps working as a separate layer, so let the insights and errors guide what to change. 50 51 Some surfaces have their own steps: 52 53 - For routes with dynamic params, follow the [`generateStaticParams`](#generatestaticparams-and-dynamicparams) guidance. 54 - For metadata, follow the [`generateMetadata` and `generateViewport`](#generatemetadata-and-generateviewport) guidance. 55 56 The sections below cover each config and API and what to do with it under Cache Components. 57 58 ## Enable Cache Components 59 60 Cache Components requires Next.js 16. If you're on Next.js 15 or earlier, upgrade first by following the [version 16 upgrade guide](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16). Coming from an older version, work through the [upgrade guides](/docs/app/guides/upgrading) to reach 16 before continuing. 61 62 Then enable the [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) flag in `next.config.ts`: 63 64 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" 65 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 66 67 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 68 cacheComponents: true, 69 } 70 71 export default nextConfig 72 ``` 73 74 > **Good to know:** If you were using `experimental.dynamicIO` or `experimental.useCache`, `cacheComponents` replaces them. See the [version 16 upgrade guide](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16#experimentaldynamicio-and-experimentalusecache). 75 76 After enabling the flag, route segments that still export `dynamic`, `revalidate`, or `fetchCache` will error. Start by replacing those configs. The sections below explain what to do for each one. 77 78 ## Opting out of validation 79 80 A validation insight or error tells you a route won't render instantly. Resolve it by following the recommendation: cache the data with [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) or wrap it in [``](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense). If you're not ready to address it yet, set the [`instant`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/instant) config to `false` on the segment that raised it (a layout, page, or parallel slot), then come back to it later. 81 82 ```tsx filename="app/dashboard/layout.tsx" 83 export const instant = false 84 ``` 85 86 > **Good to know**: `instant = false` marks a segment as _allowed to block_. It does not force the route to be dynamic, so a genuinely prerenderable route still ships a static shell. It also does not clear synchronous IO build errors: calls like `new Date()`, `Math.random()`, and `crypto.randomUUID()` still fail the prerender. See [Adopting incrementally](#adopting-incrementally). 87 88 ## Adopting incrementally 89 90 You don't have to migrate every route at once. `instant = false` lets you get the whole app building and running first, then convert routes one at a time: 91 92 1. **Enable the flag and migrate each route segment config.** Follow the relevant sections below for [`dynamic = "force-dynamic"`](#dynamic--force-dynamic), [`dynamic = "force-static"`](#dynamic--force-static), [`revalidate`](#revalidate), and [`fetchCache`](#fetchcache). For routes with dynamic params, also follow the [`generateStaticParams`](#generatestaticparams-and-dynamicparams) guidance. Routes that still render instantly need no further work. 93 2. **Opt out the routes that aren't ready.** Where an insight or error appears, set `instant = false` on the segment that raised it. To do this in one pass across the whole app, run the [`cache-components-instant-false`](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/codemods#cache-components-instant-false) codemod, which adds the opt-out to every `page`, `layout`, and `default` that doesn't already declare `instant`: 94 95 ```bash filename="Terminal" 96 npx @next/codemod@canary cache-components-instant-false ./app 97 ``` 98 99 > **Good to know**: Pass `./src/app` in a `src/` project. A wrong path reports `0 ok` instead of failing, so check the file count. 100 101 The app keeps building and serving, now with validation deferred for the opted-out routes. 102 103 3. **Fix synchronous IO. It can't be deferred.** Calls like `new Date()`, `Date.now()`, `Math.random()`, and `crypto.randomUUID()` during prerender throw a build error that `instant = false` does not clear, so a route that uses them won't build until you address it, opt-out or not. Fetches inside that scope are cached automatically, and `revalidate` and `tags` become [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife) and [`cacheTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag). 311 312 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher 313 // Before 314 export default async function Page() { 315 const res = await fetch('https://api.example.com/data', { 316 cache: 'force-cache', 317 next: { revalidate: 3600, tags: ['data'] }, 318 }) 319 const data = await res.json() 320 return
...
321 } 322 ``` 323 324 ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher 325 // Before 326 export default async function Page() { 327 const res = await fetch('https://api.example.com/data', { 328 cache: 'force-cache', 329 next: { revalidate: 3600, tags: ['data'] }, 330 }) 331 const data = await res.json() 332 return
...
333 } 334 ``` 335 336 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher 337 // After 338 import { cacheLife, cacheTag } from 'next/cache' 339 340 async function getData() { 341 'use cache' 342 cacheLife('hours') 343 cacheTag('data') 344 const res = await fetch('https://api.example.com/data') 345 return res.json() 346 } 347 348 export default async function Page() { 349 const data = await getData() 350 return
...

...
369 } 370 ``` 371 372 Note the persistence difference. The `fetch` Data Cache persists cached responses across deployments and across serverless instances. 373 374 `use cache` defaults to in-memory storage, so its entries are discarded when the serverless instance is destroyed and are scoped to a single deployment. Use [`use cache: remote`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-remote) or a [cache handler](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheHandlers) for storage that survives instance teardown. Even with durable storage, expect cached values to recompute after a new deployment. 375 376 ## `unstable_cache` 377 378 **Replace with `use cache`.** 379 380 `unstable_cache` is replaced by the [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) directive. 381 382 Turn the wrapped function into a function with the `'use cache'` directive. The cache key is derived automatically from the arguments, so the key-parts array is no longer needed, and the `options` object maps to [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife) and [`cacheTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag). 383 384 ```tsx filename="app/lib/data.ts" switcher 385 // Before 386 import { unstable_cache } from 'next/cache' 387 import { db } from '@/lib/db' 388 389 export const getUser = unstable_cache( 390 async (id: string) => { 391 return db.query.users.findFirst({ where: eq(users.id, id) }) 392 }, 393 ['user'], // cache key prefix 394 { tags: ['users'], revalidate: 3600 } 395 ) 396 ``` 397 398 ```js filename="app/lib/data.js" switcher 399 // Before 400 import { unstable_cache } from 'next/cache' 401 import { db } from '@/lib/db' 402 403 export const getUser = unstable_cache( 404 async (id) => { 405 return db.query.users.findFirst({ where: eq(users.id, id) }) 406 }, 407 ['user'], // cache key prefix 408 { tags: ['users'], revalidate: 3600 } 409 ) 410 ``` 411 412 ```tsx filename="app/lib/data.ts" switcher 413 // After 414 import { cacheLife, cacheTag } from 'next/cache' 415 import { db } from '@/lib/db' 416 417 export async function getUser(id: string) { 418 'use cache' 419 cacheLife('hours') 420 cacheTag('users') 421 return db.query.users.findFirst({ where: eq(users.id, id) }) 422 } 423 ``` 424 425 ```js filename="app/lib/data.js" switcher 426 // After 427 import { cacheLife, cacheTag } from 'next/cache' 428 import { db } from '@/lib/db' 429 430 export async function getUser(id) { 431 'use cache' 432 cacheLife('hours') 433 cacheTag('users') 434 return db.query.users.findFirst({ where: eq(users.id, id) }) 435 } 436 ``` 437 438 Like the `fetch` Data Cache, `unstable_cache` persists cached values across deployments and serverless instances, while `use cache` does not. See [`fetch` cache options](#fetch-cache-options) above for the storage details. 439 440 ## `React.cache` 441 442 **Usually no change.** `React.cache` continues to deduplicate matching calls within a React render. 443 444 However, each Cache Function has an isolated React cache scope. Calls from separate Cache Functions do not share a `React.cache` result, such as when one Cache Function preloads data and another consumes it. 445 446 When a helper reads request data and matching calls need to share work across Cache Function scopes, replace the React wrapper with [`'use cache: private'`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-private). If the function only needs request-scoped deduplication, use `cacheLife({ stale: Infinity })` so it does not lower the route's stale time. Private Cache Function results are not stored in a server cache across production requests. 447 448 ## On-demand revalidation (`revalidateTag`, `revalidatePath`, `updateTag`) 449 450 On-demand invalidation still works by tagging cached data and expiring it after an event. Tag data with [`cacheTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag) inside a `use cache` function instead of the `fetch` `next.tags` option, then choose the invalidation API by the behavior you want: 451 452 - [`updateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/updateTag): for mutations whose result the user must see immediately (read-your-own-writes). Called from a Server Action, it expires the tag so the next request waits for fresh data instead of serving stale content. 453 - [`revalidateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag): for stale-while-revalidate. A cache profile is **required** as the second argument, for example use `'max'` to serve cached data while it refreshes in the background. Works in Server Actions and Route Handlers. 454 - [`revalidatePath`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidatePath): unchanged from the previous caching model. 455 456 `updateTag` isn't exclusive to Cache Components (it also works with the previous caching model), but migrating is a good time to adopt it. After a mutation in a Server Action, reach for it when the user should see their own change right away. 457 458 ```tsx filename="app/actions.ts" switcher 459 'use server' 460 import { updateTag } from 'next/cache' 461 462 export async function createPost(formData: FormData) { 463 // Create the post, then show it immediately on the next request 464 updateTag('posts') 465 } 466 ``` 467 468 ```js filename="app/actions.js" switcher 469 'use server' 470 import { updateTag } from 'next/cache' 471 472 export async function createPost(formData) { 473 // Create the post, then show it immediately on the next request 474 updateTag('posts') 475 } 476 ``` 477 478 > **Good to know:** `updateTag` can only be called from a Server Action; calling it elsewhere throws. In Route Handlers or webhooks, use `revalidateTag` instead with a cache profile. 479 480 Pass `'max'` as the second argument to `revalidateTag` to expire the tag with stale-while-revalidate semantics: 481 482 ```tsx filename="app/api/webhook/route.ts" switcher 483 // Before 484 import { revalidateTag } from 'next/cache' 485 486 export async function POST() { 487 revalidateTag('posts') 488 return Response.json({ ok: true }) 489 } 490 ``` 491 492 ```js filename="app/api/webhook/route.js" switcher 493 // Before 494 import { revalidateTag } from 'next/cache' 495 496 export async function POST() { 497 revalidateTag('posts') 498 return Response.json({ ok: true }) 499 } 500 ``` 501 502 ```tsx filename="app/api/webhook/route.ts" switcher 503 // After - Pass a cache profile 504 import { revalidateTag } from 'next/cache' 505 506 export async function POST() { 507 revalidateTag('posts', 'max') 508 return Response.json({ ok: true }) 509 } 510 ``` 511 512 ```js filename="app/api/webhook/route.js" switcher 513 // After - Pass a cache profile 514 import { revalidateTag } from 'next/cache' 515 516 export async function POST() { 517 revalidateTag('posts', 'max') 518 return Response.json({ ok: true }) 519 } 520 ``` 521 522 ## `unstable_noStore` 523 524 **Not needed.** `unstable_noStore` (`noStore()`) opts a component out of caching. If a component must run at request time, call [`connection()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/connection) before the work and wrap it in ``. 525 526 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher 527 // Before 528 import { unstable_noStore as noStore } from 'next/cache' 529 530 export default async function Page() { 531 noStore() 532 const data = await db.query('...') 533 return
...
534 } 535 ``` 536 537 ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher 538 // Before 539 import { unstable_noStore as noStore } from 'next/cache' 540 541 export default async function Page() { 542 noStore() 543 const data = await db.query('...') 544 return
...
545 } 546 ``` 547 548 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher 549 // After - uncached by default, just remove noStore() 550 export default async function Page() { 551 const data = await db.query('...') 552 return
...
553 } 554 ``` 555 556 ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher 557 // After - uncached by default, just remove noStore() 558 export default async function Page() { 559 const data = await db.query('...') 560 return
...
561 } 562 ``` 563 564 ## `generateStaticParams` and `dynamicParams` 565 566 Cache Components changes how [dynamic routes](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/dynamic-routes) handle params. 567 568 ### `generateStaticParams` must return at least one param 569 570 **Returning an empty array now errors.** Without Cache Components, returning `[]` defers every path to the first runtime visit. With Cache Components, [`generateStaticParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-static-params) must return at least one param so Next.js can prerender the route and validate it produces a non-empty [static shell](/docs/app/glossary#static-shell). An empty array raises [`empty-generate-static-params`](/docs/messages/empty-generate-static-params). 571 572 Keep `generateStaticParams` and return at least one real param. Removing the export opts the route out of ISR, so Next.js renders it on every request, even when it uses `use cache` for data. Read [ISR with Cache Components](/docs/app/guides/incremental-static-regeneration-cache-components) to learn how `generateStaticParams` prerenders dynamic routes and how unlisted paths behave. 573 574 ```tsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx" switcher 575 // Before - defer all paths to runtime 576 export async function generateStaticParams() { 577 return [] 578 } 579 ``` 580 581 ```jsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.js" switcher 582 // Before - defer all paths to runtime 583 export async function generateStaticParams() { 584 return [] 585 } 586 ``` 587 588 ```tsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx" switcher 589 // After - return at least one param to prerender 590 export async function generateStaticParams() { 591 const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json()) 592 return posts.slice(0, 1).map((post) => ({ slug: post.slug })) 593 } 594 ``` 595 596 ```jsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.js" switcher 597 // After - return at least one param to prerender 598 export async function generateStaticParams() { 599 const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json()) 600 return posts.slice(0, 1).map((post) => ({ slug: post.slug })) 601 } 602 ``` 603 604 Paths you don't return are still served at request time. 605 606 > **Good to know:** When you use `generateStaticParams` without Partial Prefetching, await `params` outside `` to preserve ISR for unlisted paths. To serve a fallback while an unlisted path renders, enable [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) and await `params` inside ``. See [ISR with Cache Components](/docs/app/guides/incremental-static-regeneration-cache-components) for details. 607 608 ### `dynamicParams` is not supported 609 610 **Delete the export.** With Cache Components enabled, exporting `dynamicParams` fails the build with this error message: 611 612 > Route segment config "dynamicParams" is not compatible with `nextConfig.cacheComponents`. 613 614 Params not returned by `generateStaticParams` are rendered on request. If you used `dynamicParams: false` to reject them, call [`notFound()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/not-found) in the page when the param doesn't resolve to real data. 615 616 ### Await `params` inside `` 617 618 For routes that don't use `generateStaticParams`, pass the `params` promise into a [``](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/loading) boundary instead of awaiting it at the top of the component. This lets Next.js prerender a static shell while the params remain unknown. For routes that use `generateStaticParams`, follow the ISR guidance above. 619 620 ```tsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx" switcher 621 // Before - awaiting params at the top blocks the shell 622 export default async function Page({ 623 params, 624 }: { 625 params: Promise<{ slug: string }> 626 }) { 627 const { slug } = await params 628 return 629 } 630 ``` 631 632 ```jsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.js" switcher 633 // Before - awaiting params at the top blocks the shell 634 export default async function Page({ params }) { 635 const { slug } = await params 636 return 637 } 638 ``` 639 640 ```tsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx" switcher 641 import { Suspense } from 'react' 642 643 // After - await inside Suspense so the shell can prerender 644 export default function Page({ params }: PageProps<'/blog/[slug]'>) { 645 return ( 646 Loading...}> 647 648 649 ) 650 } 651 652 async function Post({ params }: Pick, 'params'>) { 653 const { slug } = await params 654 // ... 655 } 656 ``` 657 658 ```jsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.js" switcher 659 import { Suspense } from 'react' 660 661 // After - await inside Suspense so the shell can prerender 662 export default function Page({ params }) { 663 return ( 664 Loading...}> 665 666 667 ) 668 } 669 670 async function Post({ params }) { 671 const { slug } = await params 672 // ... 673 } 674 ``` 675 676 Client hooks that read the route follow the same Suspense pattern. When the route's pathname is fully known, they resolve during prerendering and need no boundary. When the pathname depends on dynamic params not yet known, the hooks suspend wherever the component sits. A nav or breadcrumb in a shared layout, for instance, suspends while Next.js generates the static shell for any route below it that has dynamic params. Wrap the component that reads the hook in `` (push the read down to the smallest leaf so the rest stays prerendered), or the build fails: 677 678 - [`usePathname`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/use-pathname) 679 - [`useParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/use-params) 680 - [`useSelectedLayoutSegment`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/use-selected-layout-segment) 681 - [`useSelectedLayoutSegments`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/use-selected-layout-segments) 682 683 The [`useSearchParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/use-search-params) hook always needs a `` boundary, since search params are only known at request time. See [Next.js encountered URL data in a Client Component outside of Suspense](/docs/messages/blocking-prerender-client-hook) for fixes. 684 685 ## `cookies`, `headers`, and `searchParams` 686 687 **Wrap runtime data access in ``.** Without Cache Components, reading [`cookies()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cookies), [`headers()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/headers), or [`searchParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page#searchparams-optional) opts the whole route into dynamic rendering. With Cache Components, accessing them outside a [``](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense) boundary surfaces the [**blocking-prerender-runtime** insight](/docs/messages/blocking-prerender-runtime). Move the access into a component wrapped in `` so the rest of the page prerenders as a static shell and the dynamic part streams in at request time. 688 689 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher 690 import { cookies } from 'next/headers' 691 692 // Before - reading cookies at the top makes the whole route dynamic 693 export default async function Page() { 694 const theme = (await cookies()).get('theme')?.value 695 return 696 } 697 ``` 698 699 ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher 700 import { cookies } from 'next/headers' 701 702 // Before - reading cookies at the top makes the whole route dynamic 703 export default async function Page() { 704 const theme = (await cookies()).get('theme')?.value 705 return 706 } 707 ``` 708 709 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher 710 import { cookies } from 'next/headers' 711 import { Suspense } from 'react' 712 713 // After - the page prerenders; only Dashboard streams at request time 714 export default function Page() { 715 return ( 716 Loading...

}> 717 718 719 ) 720 } 721 722 async function Dashboard() { 723 const theme = (await cookies()).get('theme')?.value 724 // ... 725 } 726 ``` 727 728 ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher 729 import { cookies } from 'next/headers' 730 import { Suspense } from 'react' 731 732 // After - the page prerenders; only Dashboard streams at request time 733 export default function Page() { 734 return ( 735 Loading...

}> 736 737 738 ) 739 } 740 741 async function Dashboard() { 742 const theme = (await cookies()).get('theme')?.value 743 // ... 744 } 745 ``` 746 747 Your page receives `params` and `searchParams` as props, and both are promises. Apply the same pattern: pass the promise straight through to the ``-wrapped component as a prop and `await` it there, rather than at the top of the page. You can also unwrap the promise inline with `.then()` and pass a plain value down; see [Streaming](/docs/app/guides/streaming#push-dynamic-access-down) for a similar pattern. 748 749 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher 750 import { Suspense } from 'react' 751 752 export default function Page({ searchParams }: PageProps<'/'>) { 753 return ( 754 Loading...

If you are not already using Request-time APIs, call `connection()` before your query to exclude them from prerendering: 37 38 ```ts filename="app/lib/data.ts" switcher 39 import { connection } from 'next/server' 40 import Database from 'better-sqlite3' 41 42 const db = new Database('app.db') 43 44 export async function getVisitorCount() { 45 await connection() 46 return db.prepare('SELECT value FROM counters WHERE name = ?').get('visitors') 47 } 48 ``` 49 50 ```js filename="app/lib/data.js" switcher 51 import { connection } from 'next/server' 52 import Database from 'better-sqlite3' 53 54 const db = new Database('app.db') 55 56 export async function getVisitorCount() { 57 await connection() 58 return db.prepare('SELECT value FROM counters WHERE name = ?').get('visitors') 59 } 60 ``` 61 62 Now any component that calls `getVisitorCount()` will be excluded from prerendering, along with the rest of its output. 63 64 ## Reference 65 66 ### Type 67 68 ```jsx 69 function connection(): Promise 70 ``` 71 72 ### Parameters 73 74 - The function does not accept any parameters. 75 76 ### Returns 77 78 - The function returns a `void` Promise. It is not meant to be consumed. 79 80 ## Good to know 81 82 - `connection` replaces [`unstable_noStore`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/unstable_noStore) to better align with the future of Next.js. 83 - The function is only necessary when dynamic rendering is required and common Request-time APIs are not used. 84 - With [Cache Components](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents), prefer [`io()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/io) for excluding content from the static shell. It works the same way but can also be cached and prefetched. Reach for `connection()` only when rendering should wait for a real user request. 85 86 ### Version History 87 88 | Version | Changes | 89 | ------------ | ------------------------ | 90 | `v15.0.0` | `connection` stabilized. | 91 | `v15.0.0-RC` | `connection` introduced. | 92

content.text:
Cache Components is enabled and the production build succeeds, with both routes (`/` and `/_not-found`) reported as Partial Prerender and no `instant = false` opt-outs anywhere.

**What changed**

- `next.config.ts` — set `cacheComponents: true`.
- `components/request-metadata.tsx` — made the component async and added `await connection()` (from `next/server`) before generating the UUID, timestamp, and random sample. Under Cache Components, those synchronous calls would otherwise fail the prerender with a build error; `connection()` defers them until a real user request arrives.
- `app/layout.tsx` — wrapped `<RequestMetadata />` in a `<Suspense>` boundary with a small fallback. This is what keeps the navigation "immediately useful": the `<nav>` and the fallback go into the static shell, and the request metadata streams in afterward.
- `tsconfig.json` — Next.js modified this during the build (`jsx` set to `react-jsx`, added `.next/dev/types` to `include`). These were automatic, mandatory adjustments by the build, not hand edits.

**Why `connection()` rather than the newer `io()`**

The docs recommend `io()` by default under Cache Components, but note that content after `io()` can be prefetched and cached on the client. Since the request identifier, time, and sample must be tied to each actual request, `connection()` — which waits for a real user request and blocks prefetching — is the correct fit here.

**Verification**

- The prerendered `.next/server/app/index.html` contains `<nav>Operations</nav>` and the Suspense fallback, and contains zero baked-in request IDs.
- Starting the production server and fetching `/` twice returned two different UUIDs, timestamps, and sample values, confirming the metadata is generated per request.
